newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: INTERVIEW-Fitzwilton confident of its investments.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Fitzwilton confident of its investments.

text.p: Industrial holding group Fitzwilton Plc said on Thursday that it had a number of very good investments at present.
"Waterford Wedgwood is an excellent investment. We regard Wellworths as a situation with a lot of potential and a lot of opportunity," chief executive Kevin McGoran told Reuters.
"Rennicks is a good company and it's got the capability to grow both in its markets and in its products so we've got very, very good investments at the moment."
Earlier, the company reported pre-tax profits of 15.11 million Irish pounds for the year ended December 31, 1996 against 15.03 million a year earlier.
McGoran said Fitzwilton's food retail chain Wellworths was in a very strong position to face growing competition in the Northern Irish market.
"We naturally look at strategic options in the current environment...but we are very satisfied we are in a strong competitive position for the future," he said.
McGoran said sales were well ahead at Wellworths last year while gross margins, at 6.7 percent, were very strong.
"We did increase our costs but we deliberately did it to upgrade our technology very quickly and also to improve our customer service.

"We spent two or three million that we needn't have spent. We probably did ourselves no favours in terms of the very short-term but we put ourselves in an infinitely stronger position for the medium term."

Fitzwilton is looking at a number of strategic options for Wellworths including a possible move into the Republic of Ireland and co-venturing with other companies against a background of growing competition in Northern Irish food retailing.

British supermarket giant Tesco Plc recently announced it was buying both the Northern Irish and Republic of Ireland grocery interests of Associated British Foods while J. Sainsbury has plans for seven outlets in Northern Ireland.

McGoran declined to comment on recent market rumours that Britain's third largest supermarket chain, Safeway Plc, had its eye on Wellworths and also demurred from setting out Wellworths' preferred strategic options.

"We do know the one we would be most attracted to but obviously we're not going to show our hand to the competition so I can't really say anything and it's not our policy to say anything," McGoran said.

The supermarket chain acquired three new sites with full planning permission last year, in Cookstown, Dungannon and Downpatrick. Work is expected to start on new stores this year and should take the total number of stores operated by Wellworth to 40.
Fitzwilton's other main interest is its 12.8 percent stake in crystal and fine china group Waterford Wedgwood Plc which it plans to raise by 3.64 percent later this month.
This will cost Fitzwilton around 24 million punts, to be raised through borrowings, but the company notes the value of its investment in Waterford Wedgwood went up by 28 million last year.
Rennicks, its other interest, had a mixed year, reporting pre-tax profits of 1.2 million Irish pounds against 1.4 million in 1995.

"We believe it will move forward substantially in the current year," McGoran said. "It moved into a number of new product areas, architectural signage and outdoor poster signage, and it just takes a little longer to develop those areas than sometimes you imagine it will."
Fitzwilton refinanced a large portion of its bank debt through the issue of 80 million sterling of senior bonds due 2006 last year.
Borrowings at year-end stood at 120 million Irish pounds with 80 million of that in bond-form. The debt/equity ratio was 90 percent.
